findings.summary: AxiosError.from no longer copies the original error's own properties (errno, syscall, address, port, hostname, custom fields), only message, code and name, so callers reading them get undefined.
AxiosError.from reads error.message without a null check, so a falsy error (undefined/null) throws a TypeError that hides the real failure, and a missing message becomes undefined instead of 'Error'.

cause and isAxiosError are now enumerable own properties (previously non-enumerable/prototype), showing up in Object.keys, spreads, inspect and Object.assign; from overwrites existing cause unconditionally; static error codes are now writable and enumerable.
status is set to response.status directly, so a response with no status yields undefined instead of null, breaking callers that check === null.
New specs use require('node:util/types') inside an ESM-style spec file, which may fail depending on the test runner.
No tests cover AxiosError.from's property copying, cause handling, or the null-error case, so the regressions would go unnoticed.
